choice_reasoning.expected_value_to_reviews: An email is the sole key to both review-producing engines (in-app thank-you screen + Klaviyo reminder emails). That argues for attacking motivation, not layout — exactly what 'Answer the box' does.

diagnosis.question: Why do the ~52-60% of QR scanners who land on the claim page never submit an email — and is the loss at first paint (never engage) or after engaging (form friction / declined)?
hypotheses_considered: Tonal break / thin motivation: the box that made them scan is warm & playful ('did this X make you smile?'); the page answers with a cold, transactional header ('You've Got 30% Off' / 'Enter your email to receive' / 'Send Me My Code'), so the emotional pull evaporates before they engage.
Ceiling: they never intended to reorder — a one-off gift buyer doesn't want a 'next order' discount, so nothing here is worth an email.
Distrust: unfamiliar QR-destination domain asking for an email before giving anything reads as sketchy to a fraction.
Form friction / declined: they engaged the field but gave up (typo, keyboard, second-guess).
Never reached the field: bounced/confused/slow load during the ~1.2s opening blur.
diagnosis.evidence_gathered: Analyzed session-recording METADATA (duration, keypress_count, click_count, start_url) for all 44 claim-page sessions recorded 2026-07-09..2026-07-23 via the PostHog session_recordings API (the query API is down, but recordings are a different scope and work). 23 of 44 (52%) never typed a single key; of those, 8 had ZERO clicks and 12 left within ~12s, while 6 stayed >=60s yet still never typed. I did NOT download pixel snapshots — this is metadata, not watched-frame-by-frame replay, which is the honest limit of what the API exposes without heavy blob fetches.
diagnosis.what_the_evidence_supports: The loss is dominated by people who NEVER ENGAGE the field, not by form friction — 52% never type, and the form-friction bucket (engaged-then-abandoned) is small. That makes a FIRST-PAINT motivational fix the right KIND of change and rules OUT a field-friction fix as the primary lever. The ~1.2s blur is also not the barrier: 6 never-typed sessions stayed >=60s and still never typed.
diagnosis.what_it_cannot_distinguish: Metadata cannot separate WHY they don't engage: tonal break vs ceiling vs distrust all produce the same fast no-type bounce. The durable page_viewed→email_field_engaged→email_entered split that would size never-engaged vs declined only becomes readable ~2026-08-03/05 (instrument shipped 07-20/07-22, both windows must sit on/after 07-22). So which non-engagement CAUSE dominates is genuinely unsettled this cycle.

plan.title: Answer the box: open the claim page in the box's warm voice before the transactional ask
plan.targets: Claim page: landed → gave email (first-paint engagement)
plan.mechanism: The box earns the scan with a warm, playful, emotional beat ('did this X make you smile? … there's a spud for anybud'). The page currently breaks that thread at first paint with a cold coupon header ('You've Got 30% Off' → 'Enter your email to receive' → 'Send Me My Code'). This change keeps the emotional thread continuous by opening with a short, warm line that completes the box's beat (acknowledge the gift/the smile) BEFORE stating the reward, so the visitor stays in the delighted mindset that made them pull out a phone — more people lean in and engage the field at all, instead of pattern-matching 'marketing form → close tab'. It changes only the opening kicker + reward-intro copy (one headline + one subhead). It does NOT touch layout, the email gate, the reward list, delivery, or any code.
plan.mechanism_note: Product-agnostic wording only: SKUs vary (potato, cat, dog, nurse…) and the printed % varies, so the copy must NOT hardcode 'potato/spud' and must NEVER reference or quote the printed discount number.
plan.assumed_cause: Tonal break / thin motivation at first paint: the cold, transactional opening fails to carry the box's warmth, so a share of scanners never feel pulled in enough to engage the field.

cause_verification.for: Across the 44 claim sessions recorded this window, 52% (23) never typed a key and the loss is overwhelmingly at 'never engaged' — 8 of those 23 clicked nothing at all and 12 left within ~12s. The one change that ever moved this funnel (2026-06-16) worked by changing motivation/meaning, while the one presentation reshuffle here (PR #8) went flat — the pattern favours a motivation lever. The funnel demonstrably works when the tone is warm: the box's playful voice is what earns the scan in the first place, and the page answers it with a coupon header.
cause_verification.against: I actively looked for evidence that would CONTRADICT a first-paint motivation fix, in two ways. (1) If the loss were form-friction, I would see many sessions that typed then abandoned — instead only ~21 of 44 typed at all and the never-typed bucket dominates, so a field-level fix is NOT where the loss is. (2) If the ~1.2s opening blur (the thing LAST cycle wrongly blamed) were the barrier, never-typed sessions would all be sub-2s bounces — instead 6 of 23 stayed >=60s and still never typed, and 11 sat in the 5-20s band, so people had ample time past the blur and still didn't engage. Both searches could have killed this fix; neither did. What the evidence CANNOT do is prove the tonal break (vs the ceiling or distrust) is the specific reason for non-engagement — those are indistinguishable in metadata.
cause_verification.why_for_wins: The evidence firmly establishes WHERE the loss is (first-paint non-engagement) and rules out the two causes a copy-at-the-field or blur fix would target, so this is the right KIND of change aimed at the right place. It cannot single out the tonal-break cause from the ceiling/distrust causes — so this is an explicit BET on a cause the data can't yet settle, which is exactly the small, reversible, on-brand experiment this job exists to ship. The downside is essentially nil: it changes no mechanics, breaks no promise, and is instantly revertible. This is deliberately distinct from last cycle's failure, which asserted people left during the blur while its own data showed they did not; here the data actively supports first-paint non-engagement and the fix is not premised on the blur.

plan.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: The email ask is an EXCHANGE: the visitor gives an email (a small cost + mild distrust) to get the discount code + video. The rate is the price being accepted. Converters accept because the warmth/curiosity carried over from the box makes the reward feel worth a tap; non-converters, provably, mostly never even reach the point of weighing the trade — they disengage at first paint. This change strengthens the reason to engage (keeps the warmth alive) WITHOUT removing what they must give or handing the reward over first (which the owner has ruled out).
what_would_have_to_be_true: A meaningful share of the 52% who never type are leaving because the opening feels cold/transactional rather than because they never wanted a next order (ceiling) or distrust the page.
A warmer opening line survives across all SKUs without naming a product or the printed %.
The warmth does not read as gimmicky or delay the reward enough to frustrate the discount-motivated majority.
plan.second_order_effects: The email gate is the delivery mechanism for BOTH rewards (unique single-use code via Klaviyo + email-delivered video) and enrollment for Klaviyo review-reminder emails. This change touches none of that machinery — it only rewords the opening — so no reward delivery or review path is put at risk. If it works, MORE emails means more of both review paths downstream; if it does nothing, nothing downstream changes. It does not alter what is promised, when the email is asked, or how rewards are delivered.
plan.strongest_case_against: A sceptic would say: the real reason most scanners don't give an email is the ceiling — a one-off gift buyer simply doesn't want a 'next order' discount — and no amount of warm copy fixes a wrong offer, so this is a zero-effect cosmetic tweak; also PR #8 already 'tried the claim page' and it went flat. My answer: (1) PR #8 changed structure/layout, not the opening voice — a different mechanism, and the ONE change that moved this funnel worked by changing motivation, so voice is the more promising lever, not spent ground. (2) I am not claiming this will clear the noise floor (it is labelled unmeasurable); it is a small, reversible, on-brand bet on a cause the data can't yet settle, which is exactly the compounding-experiment this job is built on. (3) If the ceiling dominates, this fix is harmless and the forthcoming never-engaged-vs-declined instrument (readable ~Aug) will tell us, informing the next, larger bet. The cost of being wrong is ~nil; the cost of doing nothing here is another idle cycle on the biggest leak.
plan.expected_effect: A plausibly small lift in landed→gave email by keeping first-paint warmth continuous, most likely inside the noise floor at this traffic. Honestly framed as a compounding bet, not a provable win.

tradeoff.gained: More scanners stay engaged at first paint and reach the email ask; if even a few more give an email, both review paths (in-app thank-you + Klaviyo reminders) get more input.
tradeoff.risked: Essentially nothing measurable is put at risk: the change touches no mechanics, no promise, no delivery. Downstream email_redirect review clicks (0 this window, 2 prior) can only rise, not fall, since the email gate is unchanged. Worst realistic case is zero effect.

plan.differs_from_past_attempt: Differs from PR #8 (recorded FLAT): PR #8 rebuilt the claim page LAYOUT/HIERARCHY (structure) — this changes only the opening VOICE (one headline + one subhead), a motivation mechanism, with no layout change. Differs from the owner-REJECTED discount-first idea: it never hands the code over before the email and never defers the gate. Differs from the owner-REJECTED printed-% idea: it never references, quotes, or compares the printed discount number. Differs from last cycle's failed diagnosis: it is not premised on the ~1.2s opening blur, and the session data actively supports (rather than contradicts) first-paint non-engagement.

alternatives_rejected: Reserved-for-you urgency cue — lower confidence (unproven no-urgency cause) and honest-urgency risks tipping pushy against the premium bar.
Maker-legitimacy trust bar — plausible but bets on a distrust cause the data can't confirm; could pair later.
Worth-it-even-once value reframe — bets directly on the ceiling cause, which if true this warm-voice change also indirectly tests at lower brand risk.
Lead-with-video second draw — a bigger reshuffle of what leads; closer to PR #8's territory and less surgical than a two-line voice change.
One-tap field microcopy — only reaches the ~48% who engage; the evidence says the loss is at never-engaged, so this targets the smaller bucket.
